purpose: Estradiol is a form of estrogen, a female hormone your body naturally makes. It is most often used to relieve symptoms of menopause, such as hot flashes, night sweats, and vaginal dryness. It may also be used to prevent bone loss (osteoporosis) after menopause or as part of hormone therapy for transgender women.
how_it_works: Your body normally produces estrogen, but levels drop significantly during menopause. Estradiol works by replacing that lost estrogen, helping bring your hormone levels back to a more comfortable range. This helps ease the uncomfortable symptoms caused by low estrogen.
common_side_effects: Breast tenderness or swelling, headaches, nausea, bloating, mood changes, spotting or irregular vaginal bleeding, and skin irritation if using a patch. These effects are often mild and may improve over time.
warnings: Estradiol may slightly increase the risk of blood clots, stroke, heart attack, or breast cancer, especially with long-term use. Tell your doctor if you smoke, have a history of blood clots, heart disease, or certain cancers. Do not use it if you are pregnant. Always use the lowest dose that works for the shortest time needed.
typical_dosing: Dosing depends on the form you use. Pills are often taken once daily. Patches are applied to the skin once or twice a week. Gels or sprays are applied daily. Vaginal creams, rings, or tablets are used for local symptoms only. Your doctor will find the right dose and form for your specific needs.
